newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended slightly firmer in drowsy pre-Christmas dealings on Tuesday as exporters sold a few dollars into the market.

The rand finished an abbreviated trading session, which finished at 1000 GMT ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday an Thursday, at 4.6865/6915 against the U.S. dollar from a 4.6920/6970 at the close on Monday.
"We had a local exporter selling a few dollars in the market," a dealer said.
"But overall it was completely dead," he added.
The rand traded in tight 4.6950-4.6845 bid band throughout the morning, touching its weakest level before the official opening as players covered short dollar positions.
Against the crosses, the rand was last a toucher stronger at 7.8396/8526 from 7.8535/8665 against sterling and at 0.3313/3318 marks from 0.3305/3310.
Dealers said the rand was seen tending weaker on Friday when the market reopened.
"There is a bit of pressure on the rand at the moment and it may move closer to 4.70," a trader said.
However, the central Reserve Bank was seen stepping into the market to stem any slide in the rand beyond that level.
"The market is so thin he (the Bank) should have no problem moving the rand," a trader said.
A lack of interest dominated the bond market on Tuesday with yields drifting slightly weaker in torpid dealings.
Traders said bonds had initially tracked the weaker rand early in the morning and had remained stuck at these levels as trade ground to a virtual halt.
"There is absolutely nothing going on...The floor looks like a morgue," one dealer said.
The key R150 bond was last at 16.14 percent from 16.11 percent on Monday.
The bond market will be closed on Wednesday and Thursday. The central Bond Exchange will also be shut on Friday with most local bond dealing rooms not opening for business.

On the money market, liquidity pressures were once again evident as the shortage rose above the 10.0 billion rand level. Reserve Bank figures show the shortage at 10.786 billion rand on Monday rising from 9.969 billion on Saturday. Three-month NCD
rates were steady at 17.40 and 17.75 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at a year high of 16.70 to 17.00 percent.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners sold a net 25.38 million rand of South African bonds on Monday after buying 2.19 million on Friday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 793.79 million rand on Monday from 2.43 billion rand on Friday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
